analysis: The PR changes only decodeVideo in MediaIngest.swift (head ~769-777, 798-801). It replaces two caseInsensitiveCompare checks with a lowercased set lookup, admitting two additional inline-video labels: data:video/mov;base64 and data:video/x-m4v;base64. The header before the first comma must match one of the four labels exactly (modulo case), so non-data: URIs (SSRF/file read) are still rejected earlier by the hasPrefix("data:") guard. The same dataFromDataURI byte cap (maxMediaDecodedBytes, preflight before allocation) still applies. MemoryBackedVideoAsset(videoData:) still sniffs the container from the bytes, so the label is not trusted for format. The same metadata-based enforceVideoLimits (duration, per-frame pixel caps) and aggregate per-request caps (count, summed frame pixels) in parts() still apply. The memory-backed asset path is unchanged, so no plaintext temp file is introduced and the T-050 mitigation is unaffected. The new accepted labels expand the input surface only to the same MP4/QuickTime parser that was already reachable, and the labels are not used for routing. One minor point: lowercased() on a Substring creates a small string whose size is bounded by the URI header. The header could be long if a client sends a long string before a comma, but the overall frame is bounded by the WS frame cap. This is not a meaningful DoS. The error message no longer echoes request-derived content, which is consistent with the existing logging policy. Nothing in this change touches the key, attestation, prefix-cache (T-041), or authorization flows. Remaining unverified: unchanged callers and tests were not reviewed, and neither was whether MemoryBackedVideoAsset rejects non-MP4/MOV containers under the new labels; that lives in an unsupplied file and is unchanged by this PR.
